subject: AWS Marketplace tile experimentation, seller playbook & AMI fallback plan
messages:
From: Sara Klein <sara@brightdataanalytics.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 04 Jul 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: Marketplace tile experiment — AMI fallback question

Hi Markus,

Thanks again for the walkthrough yesterday. We loved the proposed tile layout and the co-sell framing — quick follow-ups from our side before we pull the trigger with our procurement team: 

- On AMI fallbacks: if our preferred AMI isn't available in a region, can Redwood automatically present a quantized variant and still preserve the same SKU in the tile? Procurement is concerned about billing parity if the runtime changes.
- We also want to run a quick A/B on two tile CTAs (Start trial vs Contact sales). Any guidance on what you recommend for buyer conversion vs procurement handoff?
- Can you share a one-page seller playbook that our field team can use when customers ask about latency and compliance?

We'll need that doc for our internal enablement meeting on Monday. Attaching our initial marketplace brief for context.

Thanks,
Sara
Director of Platform Partnerships
BrightData Analytics

Attachment: BDA_marketplace_brief.pdf (application/pdf, 220 KB)

From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: Sara Klein <sara@brightdataanalytics.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 04 Jul 2026 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace tile experiment — AMI fallback question

Hi Sara — great to hear this is moving fast. Short answers up front, then a proposed plan below.

1) AMI fallback and SKU parity: Yes — Redwood will surface a compatible model variant automatically (e.g., quantized runtime) and map it to the same Marketplace SKU so the tile and purchase flow remain consistent. We treat fallback as a runtime substitution with transparent billing; the SKU remains the same but we record a runtime variant tag for telemetry and audit. Procurement examples: you will see the same SKU on invoices but the line item has a runtime_variant=quantized attribute in the invoice metadata.

2) CTA experiment recommendation: start with a 60/40 split favoring "Start free trial" (for self-serve buyer motion) and measure procurement contact rate as a secondary metric. If you see procurement-driven requests spike (users clicking Contact sales), we recommend a quick switch to emphasize Contact sales for targeted accounts.

3) Seller playbook: attached is a concise one-pager for field sellers covering key objections (latency, data residency, billing parity) plus two talking scripts (self-serve vs procurement).

Proposed immediate plan (we can finalize in a 30-min sync):
- Today (Sat): I’ll share the seller playbook + AMI fallback matrix (attached).
- Mon: quick enablement call with your field leads (30 min) — can your team do 10am PT?
- Week 1: launch 60/40 tile A/B test in two regions (us-west-2, us-east-1) with fallback enabled and telemetry on runtime_variant.

Looping in Kimberly and Tessa to scope the AMI telemetry fields and the Drive link for the experiment artifacts.

Cheers,
Markus Klein
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Attachments: 2026-07-04_BDA_tile_experiment_plan.pdf, AMI-fallback-matrix.csv

From: kimberly_park@redwood.com
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, tessa_morgan@redwood.com
Cc: rafael_mendes@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 04 Jul 2026 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Marketplace tile experiment — AMI fallback question

Thanks for the summary, Markus. Quick operational notes from product/ops side: 

- Telemetry fields: we'll emit runtime_variant, region, sku_id, and billing_tag on every purchase event. Rafael will add an invoice footnote with runtime_variant for the procurement PDF.
- AMI fallback behavior: default fallback chain will be base_AMI -> quantized_AMI -> lower_memory_AMI. We'll only swap to a different architecture at the final step; we need explicit customer opt-in for cross-arch fallback.
- CTAs: UX can support split testing with our current tile rollout mechanism; Tessa to set the experiment and provide dashboard link.

Action items: 
1) Rafael — prepare a sample invoice line that includes runtime_variant and send to Sara before Monday.
2) Tessa — draft experiment config and share the dashboard link (include audience filter for enterprise accounts).
3) Markus — confirm Monday enablement call time with Sara.

Short timeline: Rafael & Tessa will aim to have their artifacts by end of day Monday (07/06) so we can run a short internal smoke test Tues morning.

-Kimberly
Product Lead, Marketplace Enablement
Redwood Inference
